title: The Protocol of Sector Nine
premise: Casper Fairweather has spent eleven years alone on Sector Nine, tending a terraformed garden for colonists who will not arrive for another century and maintaining a beacon whose original purpose was scrubbed from every archive. When a distress signal arrives in Vessic—a language extinct since the Meridian Massacre, an event official history insists never happened—Casper discovers their own memories have been edited and that the beacon is a recorder left by massacre survivors. As a Bureau audit ship arrives to decommission the station, Casper must reconstruct the truth from the garden itself, where the dead were composted into soil, before the jump window closes and the evidence is erased forever. In the end Casper broadcasts the survivors' testimony through the beacon, chooses exile with the Bureau defector Imani rather than return to a lie, and plants the first seed of a memorial grove that outlasts them both.
about_author: Dominic Ishikawa is a former hydrologist who spent six years on remote monitoring stations in the Atacama before turning to fiction. They write quiet, character-driven science fiction about people who keep things running long after anyone remembers why.

chapters.title: The Gardener's Almanac
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A day in the life of Sector Nine: pruning nitrogen-fixers, logging weather, speaking aloud to no one. The chapter establishes the garden's beauty, Casper's loneliness, and the small ritual of the beacon's nightly pulse. Emotional beat: contentment shadowed by an ache Casper can't name—glimpses of missing time they've learned to ignore.

chapters.title: A Language With No Speakers
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The beacon receives a distress signal in Vessic, which Casper recognizes from a childhood storybook—and realizes with horror that they shouldn't know it at all. The signal contains coordinates inside the station's own footprint. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread as the first crack opens in Casper's tidy world.

chapters.title: What the Soil Remembers
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Digging at the coordinates, Casper finds bone fragments woven into the root systems—soil enriched by bodies. Their hands remember the digging though their mind doesn't. First flashback fragment: sirens, a woman's voice saying 'keep the record.' Emotional beat: grief arriving without context, like rain from a clear sky.

chapters.title: The Audit
chapters.summary: Imani Okafor's POV. Bureau auditor Imani arrives aboard the Corrigenda to decommission Sector Nine ahead of the jump window. She is efficient, rule-bound, and quietly unsettled by Casper's records—which are flawless in a way nothing real ever is. Emotional beat: two lonely professionals circling each other, suspicion laced with recognition.

chapters.title: Redacted
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Casper shows Imani the bones; Imani cross-checks and finds Sector Nine's founding crew listed as 'reassigned en bloc'—a bureaucratic ghost. Her own orders contain a clause she never read: destroy all biological material on departure. Emotional beat: dawning complicity; duty begins to taste like ash.

chapters.title: Keep the Record
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, interleaved with recovered memory. The beacon unlocks under proximity to the remains: it is a survivor-built recorder, and Casper was its keeper, memory-wiped after the massacre so they'd maintain it without knowing why. The woman's voice belongs to Dr. Sefa Vessic, the last speaker of her language. Emotional beat: identity shattering—the found family Casper lost was murdered into the garden.

chapters.title: Ninety-Six Names
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. Imani secretly restores the beacon's full archive: ninety-six victims, including children born in transit. Her supervisor orders her to file a clean report. Torn between career and conscience, she deletes the order instead. Emotional beat: love against duty crystallizes—not romance yet, but the choice of whose side she stands on.

chapters.title: Jump Window
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The Corrigenda prepares to leave; once through the jump gate, Sector Nine's records become unreachable and deniable. Imani warns Casper there are hours, not days. Casper must choose which testimony to broadcast when bandwidth allows only fragments. Emotional beat: ticking-clock desperation sharpened by tenderness between two people with nothing left to lose.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, climax. Casper hijacks the beacon and transmits Sefa Vessic's testimony in the original Vessic, aimed at every listening post in range, while Imani stalls the Corrigenda with a falsified reactor fault. Security teams board; Casper refuses to stop transmitting, reading names until they drag them away. Emotional beat: defiant grief transformed into witness—the massacre proven by being spoken.

chapters.title: First Planting
chapters.summary: Shared POV, resolution. Months later, in Bureau custody-turned-asylum after the broadcast goes public, Casper and Imani receive a parcel: seeds from listeners moved by the transmission. Cleared to emigrate together, they charter a ship to a new world and plant the first memorial grove, naming each tree for the ninety-six. Emotional beat: mourning braided with hope; a family made of two, rooted in remembrance.
